records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*

Michelangelo. Come on, up. I know you want to lie there and I get it, genuinely, but help me kick some of this debris to the perimeter so the landing area is clear. Twenty minutes of work and then you can watch the sky as much as you want.

records.response_pred:

We don't have to solve everything right now, but we can't just sit here and do nothing either. We'll figure out what to do next, but let's make sure we're doing it together.

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.

records.response_pred: Kept what for emergencies? And what emergencies are you thinking of specifically? Because if it's something we all need to know about, you probably want to let us in on it. records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
Honestly? I'd have said more, earlier. Not performed more — said more. There were moments where I knew something needed to be addressed and I waited until it was already a problem before I said it out loud. The crackers, the notebook, the raft decision — I kept trying to manage the process instead of just being straight with people from the start.

I'd also have checked in on Michelangelo more deliberately instead of waiting until he was visibly falling apart. He was giving signals the whole time and I kept treating it like something to stabilize rather than something worth actually paying attention to.

And I'd have pushed you harder, earlier — not on the hidden supplies, I didn't know about that until it was nearly over. But on the distance. You were doing useful things and I kept giving you credit for the utility while ignoring the fact that you were disappearing behind it. That's on me as much as it's on you.

What would you change? Because I notice you left that question unanswered and I'm curious whether you actually know the answer and didn't want to write it down, or whether you genuinely haven't worked it out yet.
records.response_pred:
I see. Writing things down like that, it feels like you're already thinking about what comes next. That's a big responsibility, but I think it's also a sign of how much you care.

The question you left yourself — it's a good one. We've all been so focused on surviving day to day that it's easy to lose sight of the bigger picture. But when we get back, if we get back, I think having a record like that would be incredibly helpful. It's not just about what we did, but also about why we did it, and how we could have done it better.

If I had to choose something to change, I think it would be how we handled the first few days. When resources were tight and everyone was on edge, we made some decisions under pressure that we might look back on differently. Maybe we could have handled it more carefully, with more communication, or found a way to ease the tension a bit more. 

But you know, I also think there's a part of us that wouldn't change anything. Because those first few days, even with all the stress and the fear, they were also a time when we really started to understand each other. We learned what we were capable of, and that's not something we can replicate. 

What about you? If you had to do it over, is there something specific you'd change? Or is it more about the reflections you'd have when it's all over?

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.

I'd read that report. I'm being serious.
records.response_pred:

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?

None. They didn't serve a practical purpose.
